prompt: Warren is throwing a pie party for his entire school to celebrate National Pie Day. He figures out that to feed all his guests and have a good variety of pie flavors, he should make 15 pies. The recipe he is using calls for $2\frac14$ cups of flour per pie crust. He only has 1 cup of flour in his kitchen, so he will need to buy more. Flour is sold in 5-pound bags. To figure out how many bags of flour he needs to buy, he weighs the 1 cup of flour he has. The 1 cup weighs 4.8 ounces. To make all 15 pies, how many bags of flour does Warren need to buy?

solutions.title: Cups → ounces → pounds
solutions.body:
Flour needed: $15 \times 2\frac14 = 33\frac34$ cups; to buy: $33\frac34 - 1 = 32\frac34$ cups.
Weight: $32.75 \times 4.8 = 157.2$ oz $= 157.2 \div 16 = 9.825$ lb. One 5-lb bag is not enough, two bags (10 lb) are.

**Answer: 2 bags**

solutions.title: Cups per bag
solutions.body:
A 5-pound bag is $80$ ounces, which is $80 \div 4.8 = 16\frac23$ cups. Two bags give $33\frac13$ cups $\ge 32\frac34$ cups needed, while one bag is far too little.

**Answer: 2 bags**

prompt:
Warren is making 15 pies for a pie party. He asks all his guests what their favorite type of pie is and tallies all the answers. The responses are shown in this table.

| Type of Pie | Number of Favorites |
|---|---|
| Apple | 63 |
| Cherry | 18 |
| Blueberry | 18 |
| Pecan | 9 |
| Blackberry | 27 |

If he uses the ratios of his guests' responses to determine which flavors each of his 15 pies will be, how many cherry pies should he make?

solutions.title: Fraction of responses
solutions.body:
Total responses: $63 + 18 + 18 + 9 + 27 = 135$. Cherry's share: $\frac{18}{135} = \frac{2}{15}$. Of 15 pies, that is 2 cherry pies.

**Answer: 2**

solutions.title: Guests per pie
solutions.body:
$135 \div 15 = 9$ guests per pie. Cherry has $18 \div 9 = 2$ pies' worth of fans.

**Answer: 2**

prompt:
Warren is making 15 pies for a pie party. Every guest named a favorite pie, with these results:

| Type of Pie | Number of Favorites |
|---|---|
| Apple | 63 |
| Cherry | 18 |
| Blueberry | 18 |
| Pecan | 9 |
| Blackberry | 27 |

He wants to figure out how many slices to cut each pie into to make sure everyone gets at least one slice of pie. If all cuts are made across the diameter of the pie, and every pie is cut into the same number of slices, how many slices should he cut each pie into?

solutions.title: At least 9, and even
solutions.body:
There are $135$ guests and 15 pies, so each pie needs at least $135 \div 15 = 9$ slices. Each cut across a diameter adds 2 slices, so the number of slices is even. The smallest even number $\ge 9$ is 10.

**Answer: 10 slices**

solutions.title: Check 8 and 10
solutions.body:
4 diameter cuts give 8 slices: $15 \times 8 = 120 < 135$, too few. 5 cuts give 10 slices: $150 \ge 135$ ✓.

**Answer: 10 slices**
